text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Some 1,514 people who back a "healthy style of life" took the plunge in the chilly Baltic Sea on Saturday when the air and sea temperature were around three degrees.

- Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius and IMF mission failed to reach a compromise over import tariffs early last week but high import tariffs will not help inefficient farmers and producers, the newspaper said.
- Russia decided to increase the price of crude oil to Lithuania to $135 per ton. Lithuania has been paying $15-20 less so far.
- A Lithuanian subsidiary of Siemens said the German giant has decided to suspend its investment in Lithuania as the costs were higher than in the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
- After a bull run in January, the equities market has calmed down in February.
- Six Lithuanian political parties held conferences on Saturday to discuss the March 23 local elections.
- Lithuania and Sweden are expected to sign on Monday in Stockholm a visa-free regime between the two countries.
- An office of the Lithuanian Savings Bank was robbed in Kaunas on Friday evening. Armed robbers stole $2,500 and 7,000 litas.
